name: Dashboard surface → API permission contract
purpose: Workstream C step 4 of docs/plans/2026-09-15-ultimate-platform-plan.md: the client hides, the API decides. Every row names the Dashboard module that gates a screen, the permission that module declares, the HTTP call the screen actually makes, and which roles must be refused or allowed. scripts/umipos-role-surface-gate.mjs logs in as each role and asserts the measured status against this file.

merchant.staff row created by the UX sweep with merchant.role `manager`; requires umi.user.status='active' and a password hash before it can sign in — see the gate's --roles help and the run report

client.source: apps/umi-dashboard/src/data.jsx:607 (saveMerchantSettings → PATCH /api/merchants/{merchantId}/settings is the merchant twin; the branding half is PATCH /api/{merchantRef}/admin/settings)

surfaces.note: Body `{}` is a deliberate no-op: CashReadService.updateSettings writes only the keys present. The guard runs before the handler, so a refused role is refused for the guard and an allowed role is proven to still reach the write path.

DELIBERATELY WEAKER THAN ITS MODULE. The `settings` screen is `merchant.manage` and hidden from a cashier, but this read is not only the Settings screen's: the shared merchant model (`data.jsx` `_loadMerchant`, mounted on every screen) fills the `loyalty-value` hub from it, and umi-cash's till home draws its "Recompensa activa" panel from the reference-addressed twin. Gating the read on `merchant.manage` refused a cashier a value her own screens display, so the controller enforces `loyalty.read` and the route answers 200 to a cashier. Measured, not assumed: `node scripts/umipos-role-surface-gate.mjs` reports 200 for cashier and manager on both twins. The write keeps the manager gate.

Body is the configuration already stored, read back through the same route as an allowed role, so the write is idempotent: it proves an allowed role can still save the manager screen without changing café data.

client.knownDivergence: The same screen also reads the KDS device list (data.jsx:335 → GET /api/merchants/{merchantId}/kds/devices), which the server gates on `kitchen.diagnostics` (kds-dashboard.controller.ts), not on this module's `device.enroll`. A `manager` holds kitchen.diagnostics and no device.enroll, so it can read that one list while the client hides the screen that shows it. Left as found: kds/** is outside this change, and the acceptance line (a cashier cannot reach it) holds — the cashier is refused on both routes. Reported, not silently accepted.

client.source: apps/umi-dashboard/src/data.jsx:530 (_loadOperations → GET /api/merchants/{merchantId}/operations?domain=…); the tab is operations-workspace.jsx, reached from screens/diagnostics.jsx

surfaces.note: Enforced in the service against dashboard-operations.policy.ts, one permission set per domain — the same `some()` semantics the client's hasRequiredPermission uses.

The module's gate is the `some()` of two permissions; the domain policy narrows the SAME request to `audit.read`, which is the stricter and therefore safe direction. A manager holds hardware.diagnostics and not audit.read, so this row is refused for the manager and allowed for the admin — the clearest proof that the refusal is permission-shaped, not role-shaped.
Cashier-keeps row: reportes is a module the client SHOWS to a cashier, so the server must keep serving it. Guards against over-tightening.
Cashier-keeps row: the same cash read surface this change tightened elsewhere, on the routes a cashier's own screens use.

client.source: apps/umi-dashboard/src/data.jsx:373 (_loadMerchant → GET /api/merchants/{merchantId}/settings); the module registry gates `overview` on the product alone

surfaces.note: Cashier-keeps row, and the deliberate contrast with settings.read: this is the shared café model every visible screen reads (name, locations, segments), while settings.read is the manager's branding and promo copy. Only the second one is gated.

Cashier-keeps row, and the module's own gate: `customer.read` is held by every café role (§8C grants it to cashier, staff, supervisor, manager, admin and owner), so the screen is offered and the read answers — which is the point of binding it. The route said so already (`customers.controller.ts#list` mirrors `module-registry.js`); nothing in this file did.

The `triage` module (`Atención`) gates on `customer.read` and so does the route (`customers.controller.ts#triage`), which says in its own comment that it mirrors the module. Bound here so the module's gate is a measured API decision rather than a permission nothing checks.

knownDivergences.what: umi-cash's till home reads GET /api/{slug}/admin/reward-config, and that page is shown to `STAFF` (apps/umi-cash/src/app/[slug]/(admin)/admin/page.tsx:28, layout.tsx:99-106).
knownDivergences.effect: Resolved rather than tolerated. The route used to require `merchant.manage`, which refused a till STAFF login the value its own page displays; `reward-config.read.byRef` and its merchant-scoped twin now enforce `loyalty.read`, which every role that reaches those screens holds, and the route measures 200 for a cashier. The WRITE still requires `merchant.manage`, so nothing about who may change the reward changed.
knownDivergences.decision: The read is deliberately weaker than the `settings` module that gates the screen around it: the row cites `loyalty.read` while module `settings` declares `merchant.manage`. Recorded here because that pair is the one thing a reader would otherwise read as a mistake.
